subject: Request: Canary failover charter & automatic rollback for FinPay launch
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@finpay.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@finpay.com, contracts@finpay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production rollout: canary failover charter and SLA carveout

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re green for an initial customer-facing canary for the FinPay Checkout integration the week of Dec 6. Before we flip traffic we need a written agreement on how Redwood will protect our SLA: specifically automatic fallback behavior, 'pin' semantics if a model variant is causing latency spikes, and who signs off on an emergency rollback.

Attached is a short list of the requirements our legal and ops teams expect. High-level asks:
- Automatic revert to a previously verified model variant if 99th percentile latency exceeds 750ms for >10 minutes.
- Graceful degradation mode: return truncated responses with a 503 flag when token generation is delayed beyond 2s per request.
- Pinning window: if pinned, version lock may last up to 4 hours for customer remediation, but requires written approval for >4 hours.

Can Redwood provide a canary charter we can sign off on? We’d like telemetry hooks (per-route latency histograms, token counts) delivered to our Ops team and an SLA exception form for the pin/revert workflow.

Sara
Sara Holt
Senior PM, Integrations
FinPay
[Attachment: finpay-sla-requests.pdf (PDF, 32KB)]

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@finpay.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, contracts@finpay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout: canary failover charter and SLA carveout

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I’ve sketched a proposed canary failover charter and attached a one-page draft that maps each FinPay ask to our runtime behavior. Summary below:

- Trigger: 99p latency > 750ms sustained for 10m OR error rate > 1% for 5m.
- Action: Immediate traffic shift away from canary variant to the last-stable pinned variant; we also enable a reduced-response fallback that returns a short-form message + code 503 to the client (as you requested).
- Pin semantics: Pin duration default = 2 hours; extension requires explicit written request from FinPay; on-call approval by Redwood SRE for any extension beyond 4 hours.
- Telemetry: We can stream per-route latency histograms and token usage to a pre-shared S3 endpoint or to your Datadog with a dedicated API key.

Attachments: canary_policy_draft.pdf, telemetry_playbook.xlsx, sla-exception-form.pdf

Quick question: do you want the automatic pin-unpin to be controllable by FinPay via an API key (self-serve) or partner-managed (Redwood ops)? Both are possible — self-serve speeds reaction but requires a short-term scoped credential.

I’ll loop in Naomi for the telemetry/threshold mechanics and Laura for contract signoff.

Thanks,
M

--
Michael Grant
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai
[Attachment: canary_policy_draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, Sara Holt <sara.holt@finpay.com>
Cc: ops-team@finpay.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout: canary failover charter and SLA carveout

Thanks — adding some implementation details from SRE: 

- Threshold evaluation will use a rolling 10-minute sliding window sampled every minute; 99p latency computed on completed requests only.
- Automatic rollback will initiate a traffic-shift that completes within 30s of decision; KV cache warming will be attempted on the target variant to reduce cold-start latencies.
- Reduced-response fallback: we’ll implement an explicit header X-Redwood-Fallback: true so FinPay can surface a banner to end-users.
- Audit trail: every auto-fallback, pin/unpin, and manual rollback will be logged to the customer audit log and included in monthly reports.

Note on pin duration: Operationally we prefer a default 2-hour lock to allow for investigation, and require a documented runbook and a single engineering approver for any extension. If FinPay needs longer business hours for remediation we can add an exception clause to the SLA.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: contracts@finpay.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Holt <sara.holt@finpay.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout: canary failover charter and SLA carveout

Hi Michael/Laura — legal side here. We need a short SLA exception that references these behaviors and assigns batched decision authority. Our suggested sign-off flow:
1) FinPay ops requests a pin/unpin via the designated API or email to contracts@finpay.com (we’ll confirm the exact mechanism).
2) Redwood must provide a written confirmation within 30 minutes of a manual pin request; for automatic rollbacks, Redwood must notify FinPay within 15 minutes with the event ID.
3) For any pin lasting longer than 4 hours, written C-level approval is required from both parties (email or DocuSign).

Can you produce a one-page SLA exception we can circulate? We’d like to finalize by EOD Monday to keep the Dec 6 timeline.

Thanks,
L
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, FinPay Contracts
[Attachment: sla-exception-form.pdf (PDF, 6KB)]

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: contracts@finpay.com, Sara Holt <sara.holt@finpay.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout: canary failover charter and SLA carveout

Laura/Sara — see attached 'SLA Exception — Canary Failover (FinPay)' one-pager. It matches the sign-off flow you proposed and binds the automatic triggers we described. Key calls-to-action:
- Please confirm whether FinPay will use the API key self-serve pin or route pin/unpin via your contracts mailbox. If self-serve, we’ll provision a scoped token and share instructions.
- If acceptable, we’ll put the exception into DocuSign and route to your legal for signature by EOD Monday.

I’ve also added a clause that allows us to temporarily serve truncated responses (with X-Redwood-Fallback header) while we investigate — this is to reduce user-visible tail latency without flipping the entire integration.

If I don’t hear back on the pin mechanism by Monday morning, I’ll default to partner-managed pinning and include the support SLA for manual extensions.

Best,
Michael
--
Michael Grant
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-Exception-Canary-Failover-FinPay.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]
